questions.question: In a typical quantization-aware training (QAT) pipeline, what is the primary purpose of inserting fake quantization nodes into the forward pass during training?
questions.choice_A: To simulate quantization effects on activations and weights so the model learns robustness to discretization
questions.choice_B: To reduce the number of trainable parameters and speed up backpropagation
questions.choice_C: To exactly match the numerical behavior of integer-only inference hardware
questions.choice_D: To prevent gradient flow through layers that will be quantized at inference time

questions.question: Which statement best characterizes the straight-through estimator (STE) used for discrete weight optimization?
questions.choice_A: It replaces the forward pass with a smooth surrogate but keeps the backward pass exact
questions.choice_B: It treats the non-differentiable quantizer as the identity function during backpropagation to enable gradient flow
questions.choice_C: It computes unbiased stochastic gradients by sampling from a continuous relaxation of the quantizer
questions.choice_D: It computes second-order gradients using a diagonal Hessian approximation through the quantizer

questions.question: When training with low-precision activations, why is per-channel (per-output-channel) scaling often preferred over per-tensor scaling for convolutional weights?
questions.choice_A: Per-channel scaling reduces memory footprint without affecting dynamic range
questions.choice_B: Per-channel scaling avoids the need for calibration data
questions.choice_C: Per-channel scaling better matches the channel-wise variance structure, reducing quantization error and gradient noise
questions.choice_D: Per-channel scaling allows gradients to be stored in lower precision without loss

questions.question: Which loss stabilization technique directly addresses gradient underflow/overflow when using mixed-precision training with low-bit activations?
questions.choice_A: Weight decay scheduling
questions.choice_B: Label smoothing
questions.choice_C: Dynamic loss scaling that adapts the scaling factor based on overflow detection
questions.choice_D: CutMix data augmentation

questions.question: In QAT, what is the role of learnable scale parameters in methods like LSQ (Learned Step Size Quantization)?
questions.choice_A: They regularize the logits to prevent overconfidence
questions.choice_B: They determine the quantization step size and are optimized to balance range coverage and quantization error
questions.choice_C: They remove the need for activation quantization during inference
questions.choice_D: They enforce uniform distribution of activations across bins via entropy maximization

questions.question: Which initialization strategy tends to improve stability when starting QAT from a pretrained full-precision model?
questions.choice_A: Initialize quantizer scales from random Gaussian noise to encourage exploration
questions.choice_B: Initialize quantizer scales using calibration statistics (e.g., percentile of activation/weight ranges) before fine-tuning
questions.choice_C: Initialize all weights to the nearest quantization level to minimize initial loss
questions.choice_D: Initialize the optimizer with zero momentum to avoid overshooting

questions.question: Why might adding a small L2 regularization term on the pre-quantized (float) weights improve low-bit training?
questions.choice_A: It encourages weights to grow to the extremes of the representable range
questions.choice_B: It smooths the weight distribution, helping reduce the frequency of crossings between quantization bins and lowering gradient noise
questions.choice_C: It removes the need for STE by making the quantizer differentiable
questions.choice_D: It guarantees unbiased gradients through the quantizer

questions.question: What is a common symptom of training instability specific to low-bit quantized models that you might observe in learning curves?
questions.choice_A: Monotonic increase in validation accuracy regardless of overfitting
questions.choice_B: Consistent underfitting even with very large models
questions.choice_C: High-frequency oscillations in training loss with intermittent gradient overflows or NaNs
questions.choice_D: Perfect alignment of training and validation losses throughout training

questions.question: Which optimizer setting is generally recommended to mitigate noisy gradients arising from quantization?
questions.choice_A: Increasing momentum or using adaptive optimizers with tuned beta parameters to smooth updates
questions.choice_B: Using a very high fixed learning rate to escape discrete local minima
questions.choice_C: Disabling weight decay to prevent interaction with quantization scales
questions.choice_D: Turning off gradient clipping to preserve gradient magnitude

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of weight clipping when training binary or ternary networks?
questions.choice_A: To expand the dynamic range represented by the quantizer
questions.choice_B: To prevent weight magnitudes from drifting far from the representable discrete set, stabilizing the STE gradients
questions.choice_C: To eliminate the need for batch normalization layers
questions.choice_D: To enforce sparsity by zeroing out small gradients

questions.question: Compared to deterministic rounding, what is a potential advantage of stochastic rounding in low-precision training?
questions.choice_A: It yields exact gradients through the quantizer in expectation
questions.choice_B: It reduces gradient variance by making the forward pass fully deterministic
questions.choice_C: It provides an unbiased quantization error in expectation, which can improve convergence in very low precision regimes
questions.choice_D: It eliminates the need for any regularization

questions.question: Which diagnostic would most directly reveal if a particular layer is a bottleneck due to quantization during QAT?
questions.choice_A: Per-layer gradient norm statistics and activation saturation histograms under fake quantization
questions.choice_B: Overall training accuracy after the first epoch
questions.choice_C: Wall-clock training time per batch
questions.choice_D: Model size on disk

questions.question: In practice, why is a warm-up phase for the learning rate especially beneficial when transitioning a pretrained model to low-bit QAT?
questions.choice_A: It allows the optimizer to quickly jump to a sharply quantized optimum
questions.choice_B: It gives the model time to adapt to quantization noise and scale parameters before receiving large gradient updates
questions.choice_C: It prevents any need for STE in early training
questions.choice_D: It guarantees convergence to the same solution as full-precision training

questions.question: What is a common adjustment to batch normalization (BN) when training quantized models?
questions.choice_A: Removing BN entirely to avoid extra state
questions.choice_B: Freezing BN statistics after a brief calibration or using per-channel affine parameters tuned for quantization ranges
questions.choice_C: Replacing BN with dropout to reduce overfitting
questions.choice_D: Using group normalization with no affine parameters in all cases

questions.question: Which variant of STE attempts to reduce bias by scaling the backward pass derivative according to the quantization step size or clipping range?
questions.choice_A: Identity STE with no clipping
questions.choice_B: Hard tanh surrogate without gradient scaling
questions.choice_C: Scaled STE as used in LSQ, where gradients are proportional to 1/step-size and clipped to the quantization support
questions.choice_D: Reinforce-based estimator with score function

questions.question: How can loss-aware regularization help when optimizing under quantization constraints?
questions.choice_A: By adding terms that encourage weights and activations to align with quantization levels, reducing mismatch between training and inference losses
questions.choice_B: By penalizing large batch sizes to control gradient variance
questions.choice_C: By forcing all layers to share a single global scale
questions.choice_D: By disabling data augmentation to reduce noise

questions.question: When measuring training instability in low-bit models, what does a sharp increase in activation saturation events indicate?
questions.choice_A: Underfitting due to too small a model
questions.choice_B: Excessive weight decay shrinking scales too quickly
questions.choice_C: Quantizer ranges or scales are too tight, causing frequent clipping and information loss
questions.choice_D: Data preprocessing mismatch only

questions.question: Which technique helps decouple the optimization of weight values from their scales in QAT to improve stability?
questions.choice_A: Coupling all scales through a global L1 penalty
questions.choice_B: Two-stage training: first freeze scales while adapting weights, then unfreeze scales for joint finetuning
questions.choice_C: Using a single shared scale across all layers to simplify optimization
questions.choice_D: Eliminating momentum so scales adapt faster

questions.question: Why might gradient clipping be more important in quantized training compared to full precision?
questions.choice_A: Because quantized models always have larger gradients
questions.choice_B: Because the STE can produce large or unstable gradients near quantization thresholds, and clipping prevents catastrophic updates
questions.choice_C: Because clipping increases the representable dynamic range of activations
questions.choice_D: Because clipping removes the need for loss scaling

questions.question: What is a practical criterion for deciding per-layer bit-width allocation during mixed-precision QAT?
questions.choice_A: Assign more bits to layers with the smallest parameter counts
questions.choice_B: Assign more bits to layers that show high Hessian sensitivity or large quantization-induced loss increase, keeping others low-bit
questions.choice_C: Assign the same bit-width to all layers to simplify deployment
questions.choice_D: Assign the most bits to layers closest to the output only
